articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped a record-breaking 200 security holes like confetti at a hacker convention. When AI starts hunting bugs, apparently it finds them faster than we can spell 'CVE'.

articles.title: Microsoft's worst 'Nightmare' unleashes BitLocker bypass 0-day
articles.summary: ShinyHunters went full shopping spree on 100+ orgs using an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day. Universities got hit hardest because apparently higher education means lower security standards.

articles.title: VRChat says somebody faked a breach notice with the Maine AG's office
articles.summary: Another day, another BitLocker bypass from the prolific Nightmare researcher. Microsoft's encryption is starting to look more like a polite suggestion than actual security.

articles.title: Segmentation Works for OT If Operators Are Paying Attention
articles.summary: Max-severity Ivanti flaw got exploited within 24 hours of disclosure. Attackers had their homework done and their exploits ready—this is why we can't have nice things.

articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually published AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets on GitHub like it's their personal blog. Congress is demanding answers while we're demanding better contractors.

articles.title: Cybercriminals claim breach of Oracle PeopleSoft servers at 100-plus organizations | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nearly a million passports and IDs just hanging out on the public internet like a digital yard sale. Someone typed a few characters into their browser and found an identity theft goldmine.

articles.title: Nearly a million passports and photo IDs were left unprotected on the public internet
articles.summary: South Korea just slapped Coupang with a $409 million fine for leaking 33 million customers' data. Finally, a country that puts actual teeth behind their privacy laws.

articles.title: Phishing Attack Volume Down 20%, but Risk Still Rising
articles.summary: Congress keeps kicking the Section 702 surveillance can down the road while EFF demands warrant requirements. It's warrant requirement or bust time—no more warrantless spying on Americans.

articles.title: ‘News’ Site Keeps Hallucinating EFF Staffers
articles.summary: California wants to ban surveillance pricing where corporations charge you different amounts based on stalking your digital footprint. Finally, someone noticed the creepy personalized price tags.

articles.title: A Point-by-Point Breakdown of Trump’s Failed Iran War Objectives
articles.summary: Hakeem Jeffries finally grew a spine and rallied Dems against extending domestic spy laws. About time centrist Democrats remembered they're supposed to protect civil liberties, not enable surveillance states.
